#### 1. X-linked recessive ocular albinism  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.787)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9824585, Reactome:R-HSA-375280, Reactome:R-HSA-416476)

**Proposed mechanism:** Pathogenic variant in GPR143 —DISRUPTS→ GPR143 (HGNC:4365); GPR143 (HGNC:4365) —DISRUPTS→ Melanogenesis and melanosome maturation (REACT:R-HSA-1927625); Melanogenesis and melanosome maturation (REACT:R-HSA-1927625) —LEADS_TO→ Nystagmus (HP:0000605); Melanogenesis and melanosome maturation (REACT:R-HSA-1927625) —LEADS_TO→ Ocular albinism (HP:0001050). Pathogenic variants in GPR143 disrupt melanogenesis and melanosome maturation, leading to both nystagmus and ocular albinism.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of distinct causal genes for each disease, or demonstration that mutations in GPR143 lead to gain-of-function or dominant-negative effects in one disease while causing loss-of-function in the other, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: A pathogenic variant in GPR143 with a minor allele frequency > 0.01 in gnomAD would challenge its role as a rare disease-causing gene.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared molecular basis of these ocular disorders mediated by GPR143 could pave the way for targeted therapies aimed at restoring normal melanogenesis or melanosome function, potentially ameliorating visual deficits in both conditions.

#### 2. Tietz syndrome  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.435)

Loss-of-function variants in GPR143 disrupt melanocyte function, leading to nystagmus. Similarly, loss-of-function variants in MITF disrupt melanocyte development, leading to albinism. Both genes converge on the critical pathway of melanocyte development and pigmentation, explaining the mechanistic overlap.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of a pathogenic variant in GPR143 or MITF with a frequency >0.1% in gnomAD would cast doubt on their role as primary causal genes for these rare diseases. _(variant: Exomes or Genomes)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared pathway of melanocyte development and pigmentation offers potential therapeutic targets for both congenital nystagmus and albinism syndromes, possibly through gene therapy or small molecule modulators of pigmentary processes.
